details:
EarthSound Explorer – The Earth Information Jukebox

EarthSound Explorer is an interactive web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “The Earth Information Jukebox.” The project explores an alternative way of understanding Earth science information by transforming environmental data into musical sounds.

Traditionally, environmental changes are communicated through charts, graphs, and numerical datasets. Although useful, these formats may be difficult for some people to interpret. EarthSound Explorer makes this information more engaging and accessible through sonification, the process of converting data into sound.

The application allows users to explore three environmental categories: global temperature change, atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂), and Arctic sea ice. Each selected data value is mapped to a musical pitch using JavaScript and the Web Audio API. As users play the sonification, they can hear variations in the data through changing musical tones.

The website also includes interactive charts and data tables, allowing users to compare the audio experience with visual representations of the information. Playback controls such as Play, Pause, and Stop, along with adjustable speed and volume, provide an interactive experience.

The project is built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It runs directly in a web browser and uses the browser's built-in Web Audio API to generate sounds without requiring an external audio service.

EarthSound Explorer demonstrates how technology and creativity can make scientific information more engaging. It aims to encourage curiosity about our planet and offer users another way to explore environmental trends.

Data transparency: The current version uses illustrative, unverified sample data for demonstration purposes. These values are not official NASA measurements or live NASA data.
